axes.model_access:
**Same model entry point as the CLI form: supports cloud and local LLMs, and can connect to almost any model.**

**The README's current recommended list is stuck on the previous generation of models** (Claude 3.7 Sonnet / DeepSeek R1 / OpenAI o1, etc.).

The state of that README matches the project's release state.

**This project has not shipped a release in 13 months.**

So verify this list yourself when using it as a reference.
axes.runtime:
**It is not an editor plugin; it is a usage mode.**

Aider watches your files in the background.

You add AI comments in any IDE or text editor, and it responds.

The official docs page is literally titled "Aider in your IDE".

But the implementation runs **Aider's own browser UI**.

**This is a different form factor from the "editor extension" approach of Cline / Codex.**
axes.local_files:
Watch mode monitors changes to **all files inside the git repository** and responds to AI comments.

**Official wording**: "watch all files in your repo"

(from `--watch-files` in the official `docs/usage/watch.html`.)

Scope is constrained by `.gitignore` / `.aiderignore`.

- `--aiderignore` specifies the ignore file; defaults to `.aiderignore` at the git root
- `--subtree-only` considers only the current subtree

The repository must be a git repository. The official `docs/git.html` states: without git, it first asks whether to create one.

**The core Repo Map capability is exactly the same as in the CLI form** — the same mechanism of the same project; official docs at `docs/repomap.md`.

It provides context via "a concise map of your whole git repository".

This map contains the most important classes and functions along with their types and call signatures.

The map is attached to every change request.

**Its second purpose is especially useful in watch mode**: when writing new code, it helps reuse libraries, modules and abstractions already in the codebase.

Supports 100+ programming languages.

**The map's token budget is controlled by `--map-tokens`.**

**Refresh frequency is controlled by `--map-refresh`**, with values auto/always/files/manual.

Actual time and token cost on large repos: **the official docs give no numbers, and this site has not run measurements**.
axes.background:
**The Aider process must stay resident** to respond to comments — this is not the same thing as "background cloud tasks".

**When the process exits, watch stops.**

There is also no cloud form that keeps running after the client closes.
axes.tools:
The two core capabilities are file editing and Git auto-commit, the same mechanisms as in the CLI form.

**Lint / test commands can be configured to run automatically**.

Official docs at `docs/usage/lint-test.html`.

- `--lint-cmd` / `--auto-lint`: by default run lint on edited files
- `--test-cmd` / `--auto-test`
- `/run`: run a shell command
- `/web`: fetch a web page and convert it to markdown
- `/paste`: paste an image

In watch mode, you can drag files from the editor into the agent panel, or send the editor selection to the chat.

Adding a `# AI` comment in a file adds that file to the chat.

**No built-in MCP support** — neither the official options table nor the docs-site navigation has any MCP entry (checked `config/options.html` and the docs directory).

So you cannot connect MCP servers.
axes.context:
Repo Map provides a whole-repo structural view, attached to every request; see local_files.

**Context overflow is handled by "summarization compression" rather than simple truncation.**

The official option `--max-chat-history-tokens` is described as:

**Official wording**: "Soft limit on tokens for chat history, after which summarization begins"

That is, summarization begins once the soft limit is exceeded; summaries are generated by `--weak-model`.

`--map-tokens` controls the repo map's token budget.

Each model's context window and cost come from `--model-metadata-file`.

Within a session, `/tokens` shows usage.

To free space there are also `/drop`, `/clear`, `/reset`.

**No cross-launch restoration by default** (`--restore-chat-history` defaults to False).

Chat history is written to `.aider.chat.history.md` by default.
axes.permissions:
**Auto-commit is on by default.**

The official `--auto-commits` defaults to True: every edit is committed with a sensible commit message.

`--dirty-commits` defaults to True: existing uncommitted changes are committed first, separating your changes from AI changes.

The undo path is **git itself** (`/undo`).

**A confirmation step exists.**

The official docs provide `--yes-always` (alias `--yes`).

**Official wording**: "Always say yes to every confirmation"

Meaning: by default it asks about certain operations; only with this flag does it go fully automatic.

`--dry-run` previews without changing files.

Commits skip pre-commit hooks by default (`--git-commit-verify` defaults to False, i.e. it uses `--no-verify`).

**No sandboxing mechanism** (the official options table has no sandbox entry).

Watch mode reuses the same coder.

The official watch page says it uses `/undo` to revert and `/tokens` to manage context.

So the auto-commit and confirmation mechanics above apply equally.

**The combination of a resident process + auto-commit + explicit flags needed to avoid asking is high-risk.**
axes.fit:
**Fits** two kinds of people:

- those who work comfortably in any editor and don't want to switch to a dedicated agent UI
- those who want the lightweight "add a comment → automatic response" interaction

sectionTitles.它在 IDE 形态里的位置: Where it sits among IDE forms

sections.它在 IDE 形态里的位置:
The IDE form has four variants so far, and this entry is the fourth:

| Form | Representative | Essence |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone editor | Zed | ships a full editor |
| Native desktop app | Cline Desktop | does not attach to an editor |
| Editor extension | Codex IDE, Copilot, Cline extension | installed into an existing editor |
| **Resident watch mode** | **Aider** | **runs outside the editor, watching file changes** |

**What makes Aider special**: it does not enter the editor; it watches the changes you make in whatever editor you use.

### The official docs' wording

The official docs page is titled "Aider in your IDE".

The English original:

```
Aider can watch your files and respond to AI comments
you add in your favorite IDE or text editor.
```

**Note the last half-sentence**: `or text editor`.

Even a plain text editor works, because it watches file changes, not editor APIs.

**But the interface is still Aider's own browser UI**, not an in-editor inline display.
sections.与 CLI 形态的关系:
| | [CLI](../../coding/products/aider-cli.md) | Watch mode (this entry) |
|---|---|---|
| Interaction | terminal chat | add AI comments |
| Interface | terminal | Aider's browser UI |
| Process | ends with the session | **must stay resident** |
| Repo Map | yes | yes (same capability) |

**One project, two usage modes** — not two implementations.
sections.关键风险：常驻 + 自动提交:
This entry needs special attention to a combination of three factors.

| Factor | Status |
|---|---|
| Resident process | must keep running to respond |
| Auto-commit | AI changes go straight into git history (`--auto-commits` defaults to True) |
| Ask each time | there is a confirmation flag `--yes-always` (off by default) |
| | **it asks about certain operations by default** |

**All three combined, the risk is higher than the manually launched CLI usage.**

The three are: resident process, auto-commit by default, and needing an explicit `--dry-run` or disabled auto-commit to preview.

**Advice**: when first using watch mode, try it in a small repository and make sure git status is clean first.
